summary_en: This phase 1/phase 2 pilot feasibility trial tests consolidation treatment after enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab in people with muscle invasive bladder cancer that cannot be removed by surgery, has spread to nearby lymph nodes, or has spread to a limited number of distant sites. Patients with remaining disease receive either chemoradiation (IMRT or VMAT, 55 Gy in 20 fractions) to the bladder with or without pelvic lymph nodes, or radical cystectomy, based on shared decision-making, and metastatic sites may receive SBRT before observation or maintenance pembrolizumab. The main outcome measure is not stated; the record describes the study's goals as safely eliminating residual disease and delaying progression.
summary_es: Este ensayo piloto de viabilidad en fase 1/fase 2 evalúa un tratamiento de consolidación después de enfortumab vedotina más pembrolizumab en personas con cáncer de vejiga que invade el músculo, que no puede extirparse con cirugía, que se ha extendido a ganglios linfáticos cercanos o que se ha extendido a un número limitado de sitios distantes. Los pacientes con enfermedad residual reciben quimiorradioterapia (IMRT o VMAT, 55 Gy en 20 fracciones) a la vejiga con o sin ganglios pélvicos, o cistectomía radical, según una decisión compartida, y los sitios metastásicos pueden recibir SBRT antes de observación o pembrolizumab de mantenimiento. La medida de resultado principal no se indica; el registro describe como objetivos del estudio eliminar de forma segura la enfermedad residual y retrasar la progresión.
who_for: Adults 18 or older who can understand and sign written consent.
Muscle invasive bladder cancer at diagnosis, with specified clinical stage criteria.
Radiographic complete or partial response after 3 to 9 cycles of enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab.
If metastatic after treatment, 5 or fewer sites, all outside the brain.
Candidate for pelvic radiation or cystectomy, ECOG 0-2, and life expectancy over 6 months.
not_for: Prior radiation with a field that overlaps the planned radiation field.
Any small cell component, or mostly sarcomatoid or plasmacytoid histology.
Other active cancer, or clinically relevant cancer within the past 2 years.
Uncontrolled HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or conditions that increase radiation sensitivity.
